title: Parāpraveśikā — Entry into the Supreme
author: Ascribed to Kṣemarāja
text:
The Parāpraveśikā is a sūtra-text of the recognition school, ascribed by tradition to Kṣemarāja and transmitted in the Kashmirian recension. Its nine songs treat entry (praveśa) into the Parā — the Supreme — as the fruit of a vow that binds deity and doctrine in a single commitment: the consciousness venerated is the consciousness realized. The verses move from invocation through the forms of that entry, keeping the practical and the metaphysical welded, as this tradition always does.

Its juice: entry is not travel to another place. The Parāpraveśikā's argument is that the Supreme is entered precisely where one already stands, once the vow — and the recognition it secures — is taken seriously; the text is a map of a distance that collapses under attention.
